A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DarwinTOD and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H. Corresponding material can be matched reliably despite additions, renumbering, and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original DarwinTOD benchmark results, ablations, evolutionary analyses, and human evaluations in Sections 4–5 and Appendices C–E.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds evaluations on newer dataset variants, sequential domain learning, and autonomous simulated-user conversations.

M1.justification: The ESB, peer-critique pipeline, fitness-based selection, evolutionary operators, and Algorithms 1–3 remain unchanged. The added generative UserSim prompt supports a new evaluation environment without revising the retained strategy-learning algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 substantially expands input conditions through SGD-X schema variations and fully autonomous UserSim conversations, alongside the retained benchmark and human evaluations. MultiWOZ 2.4 adds corrected annotations within existing domain coverage; it does not introduce new domains.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in the corresponding main, few-shot, zero-shot, and ablation comparisons. New Tables 11–12 report standalone DarwinTOD backbone results, while Table 13 compares training orders for the same method.

E3.justification: New Appendix C.6 specifies alphabetical introduction of seven domains followed by domain combinations, without resets or replay, and final full-test evaluation using Qwen3-4B. Appendix E.3 adds 500 GPT-5.1 simulated dialogues with generated subsequent utterances and evaluation at dialogue completion. MultiWOZ 2.4 additionally introduces corrected evaluation annotations; existing protocols remain intact.

E4.justification: v2 adds targeted tests of schema-variation robustness, resistance to forgetting under sequential domain exposure, and sustained improvement during autonomous simulation. Existing component ablations, initialization and temperature analyses, efficiency experiments, and Appendix H case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version documents repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests for the reported improvements. The existing expert-agreement statistic, Fleiss’ kappa of 0.73, is unchanged; the added experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: New Tables 11–13 and 18 add substantial results: GPT-5.1 obtains 121.28 Combine on MultiWOZ 2.4; Qwen3-8B obtains 93.95 on SGD-X; sequential Qwen3-4B training yields 114.91 on MultiWOZ 2.0; simulated-user success rises from 87.61 to 92.01 across study halves. Existing results remain unchanged. These are additional experimental conditions, rather than revised same-setting performance.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation, fitness and selection equations, entropy definition, and Appendix A’s noise and convergence derivations are unchanged. The new forgetting discussion supplies an interpretation rather than an additional mathematical argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: population-based strategy evolution, autonomous dual-loop improvement without task-specific fine-tuning, and state-of-the-art performance. Added evaluations support these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds focused BLEU/GLEU caveats, explicit latency and resource limitations, deployment recommendations, and interpretations of the new robustness and simulation results. Existing mechanism explanations remain. Some added interpretations exceed the evidence, particularly inferring per-domain forgetting resistance from final aggregate scores.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the stated anonymous code reference with a named GitHub repository and supplies the response-generating UserSim prompt in Appendix G.5. Existing hyperparameters, software, and hardware disclosures remain unchanged. Repository availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds Lee et al. (2022) for SGD-X and Ye et al. (2022) for MultiWOZ 2.4. The related-work discussion and positioning against earlier dialogue and evolutionary-agent research otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized wording and hyphenation edits, a shortened author block, acknowledgments, and added appendix subsections. The overall narrative and Appendix A–H organization remain stable. Appendix D.3.4 also duplicates an existing deployment paragraph.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 11–13 and 18 and relocates existing displays as text reflows, including separating the two strategy-embedding plots across pages. Existing figures retain their content and design, and the two-column presentation remains.

improvement.justification: The added robustness, sequential-learning, and simulation experiments provide useful evidence, while metric caveats and the simulator prompt improve transparency. Benefits are limited by aggregate-only forgetting evaluation and underspecified simulated quality/satisfaction ratings. Appendix E.3 also incorrectly describes a larger turn reduction: Tables 17–18 show 2.27 simulated versus 2.44 real-user turns. Together with duplicated deployment prose, these weaknesses temper an otherwise useful extension.
